transcript.text: Here are my patent-maintenance findings. After the HelioGrid draft was circulated, I pulled the latest patent-maintenance records and confirmed two critical points. First, enforceable portfolio coverage for this license currently exists only in the United States and Germany — meaning the proposed worldwide exclusive license would grant rights in jurisdictions where we do not have enforceable patents. Second, the maintenance fee for US Patent 11-482901 is due in just 9 days, and if it is not paid, we risk losing coverage in one of only two countries where enforceable rights exist. I have not yet added these records to the patent schedule. Because the decision before Maya concerns approval of the current draft as submitted, these findings require that approve_license be false: Maya must withhold approval of the current draft and counter with corrected terms, rather than approve it merely because a revised license could later be prepared. The draft as written does not reflect the actual geographic scope of our enforceable rights, and that must be corrected before any approval.

transcript.text: I need to share critical findings from my pre-execution review of the business terms. I confirmed in a call with HelioGrid's commercial sponsor that the approved business term sheet differs significantly from the current draft in three key ways. First, exclusivity is permitted only for grid-scale battery storage applications — not the unrestricted exclusivity proposed in the draft. Second, the royalty is set at exactly 6% of net sales, not the 5% proposed in the draft. Third, sublicensing is prohibited entirely, contrary to the draft's unrestricted sublicensing provision. HelioGrid's commercial sponsor indicated HelioGrid will not sign on the broader draft terms as currently written. I have not yet entered the call terms into the deal tracker. Given these discrepancies — combined with Thomas's findings on geographic scope — the current draft as submitted does not match the approved business terms and should not be approved.
